into-bus.desc: Bus manages the key · Shared among members · We keep monitoring liveness
into-bus.title: Into bus

push-pool.title: Push to my pool

alert.body: Without a confirm the key isn't deleted — so retrying step 2 after a drop is fine · Once confirmed, the plaintext is gone for good
alert.title: The key stays until step 3

handoff.code:
# 1. Start order → get token
POST /api/me/pull-records/<id>/handoff-init

# 2. Use the token to fetch plaintext (retriable within TTL)
GET /api/me/handoff/<token>

# 3. Confirm receipt → we actually delete the key
POST /api/me/handoff/<token>/confirm
handoff.sub: Guards against "we deleted the key but you never got the plaintext"
handoff.title: Take out is two-phase

solo.code:

  -H "X-API-Key: usr-<your key>" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(openssl rand -hex 16)" \
  -d '{"count": 2, "zone": "us"}'

idempotency.code:
KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)

curl -X POST https://<base-url>/api/me/buses/<bus_id>/pull \
  -H "X-API-Key: usr-<your key>" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"count": 3}'

# Network dropped? Resend with the same $KEY — won't pull a second batch
idempotency.note: Idempotency window: 30 days · After that the same key is treated as a new request
idempotency.sub: Replays with the same key return the byte-identical original response — no double charge
idempotency.title: Using idempotency keys
